This is a trusted-module contract, not an unprivileged interface. Do not restore the historical kfree_skb hook explicitly removed by c1e292ea7c7c; native skb tracing remains.

records.rationale: Retain socket-create, inet-create and uplink notifications for common vendor policy. Preserve native protocol/security/BPF checks. Keep existing bool error-flag API. Remove duplicate net.h include in IPv6. records.rationale: Retain restricted inet-create/release and window hooks, RTT/UDP enqueue observers and skb-build initialization hooks. Callbacks preserve vendor metadata/policy source contracts on existing common networking code. Default bodies are exactly LTS after hook removal. Restricted window hook follows tp->rcv_wnd update but precedes advertised-window clamping, so a module may deliberately make advertisement differ from stored window; preserve ACK placement and explicitly leave policy consistency to trusted callbacks. Build hooks run after skb finalization; no new public packet format or hardware platform.

records.rationale: Retain restricted BPF skb-load override for module traffic-accounting extensions. With handled=0, the complete original LTS bounds/copy/error-zeroing path runs; handled!=0 returns callback status before native checks. This deliberately delegates output initialization, length/offset handling and error clearing to a trusted registered module, which can otherwise expose stale bytes or corrupt memory if incorrect. No consumer absence is inferred and no safety guarantee is made for vendor callbacks; common source-hook compatibility is the reason for retaining this override.

records.rationale: Retain receive-socket and task-classid hooks plus GPL wrapper so modules can preserve classification across SCM_RIGHTS transfer or network-thread context. Full default functions equal native after removing hooks. Classid override changes classification and must honor intended cgroup isolation; it does not change credential checks on descriptor transfer. Wrapper retains configuration guards and does not require historical binary struct layouts.

records.rationale: Retain unconditional tcp_sync_mss export instead of EXPORT_IPV6_MOD because the SDK has IPV6=y and rebuilt vendor modules may adjust TCP MSS. Entire native implementation remains identical. This is a real module source interface, not ABI padding; callers retain locking/input responsibilities and can influence transport behavior.

records.rationale: Retain page_pool memory-provider validation hook for const ops residing in module rodata. Default validated=false preserves native is_kernel_rodata check, DMA-map/sync prerequisites, init error handling and cleanup; registered callbacks may explicitly bypass the core-rodata test. This weakens that defensive origin check when used: kernel code does not independently establish read-only module storage or module lifetime. Trusted callbacks must validate both and must not approve writable/dangling ops. Retained for source module customization in common configured page-pool infrastructure, not a new physical platform; actual provider/runtime use is unverified.

target_evidence: Networking stack, TCP/UDP, CFG80211 and page-pool infrastructure are common SDK build paths. Vendor callbacks and exports are retained as explicitly requested module-source/runtime customization, without requiring a discovered proprietary consumer or enabling a future platform. Historical KMI fields and dumps are separately omitted.
limitations: Callbacks can intentionally override native validation/policy. Specific BPF copy, page-pool origin/lifetime, packet-list isolation and TCP-window risks are explicit per candidate.
Default-path source equality does not prove callback behavior, concurrency, memory ownership, security policy or runtime performance.
Focused cleanup test executes final labels with release marker, not real sockets or deallocation.
All inputs are local. No external specification, remote resource, Android OS build, boot or flash.
